documents.act_title: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan (1973)
documents.section_title: Jurisdiction of High Court (Constitutional Writ Petitions)
documents.chapter: Part VII, Chapter 3: The High Courts
documents.punishment: Judicial review orders: Writs of Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, Prohibition, and Quo Warranto.
documents.summary_plain: Provides direct constitutional access to the High Court when a person's fundamental rights are violated, or when an administrative official or state authority acts without lawful authority or fails to perform a legal duty. Also used for Habeas Corpus to recover missing or unlawfully detained persons from police custody.
documents.summary_urdu: ہائی کورٹ کا رٹ دائرہ اختیار (آرٹیکل 199)۔ بنیادی حقوق کے تحفظ، سرکاری افسران کی غیر قانونی کارروائیوں کو کالعدم قرار دینے، اور حبسِ بے جا (غیر قانونی پولیس حراست سے بازیابی) کے لیے آئینی درخواست۔
documents.statutory_text: Article 199(1): Subject to the Constitution, a High Court may, if it is satisfied that no other adequate remedy is provided by law: (a) on the application of any aggrieved party, make an order: (i) directing a person performing within territorial jurisdiction functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation, a Province or a local authority, to refrain from doing that which he is not permitted by law to do, or to do that which he is required by law to do; or (ii) declaring that any act done or proceeding taken has been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; (b) make an order directing that a person in custody within the territorial jurisdiction be brought before it so that the Court may satisfy itself that he is not being held in custody without lawful authority (Habeas Corpus)...
evidence_required: Proof that no other adequate, efficacious alternate legal remedy exists under normal statute
Documentary proof of unlawful government action, notification, or omission
Affidavit of the petitioner affirming bona fides and personal aggrievement
For Habeas Corpus: Details of date, time, and police personnel involved in unlawful detention
practical_steps: Engage an Advocate of the High Court to draft a Constitutional Writ Petition under Article 199.
Attach attested copies of representations made to authorities and proof of their refusal or inaction.
For missing/illegally detained persons, file Urgent Habeas Corpus petition; Court appoints a Bailiff to raid the police station immediately.
High Court issues notices and may grant interim stay against illegal executive actions.
documents.forum_court: High Court (Lahore High Court, Sindh High Court, Peshawar High Court, Balochistan High Court, Islamabad High Court)

documents.act_title: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan (1973)
documents.section_title: Right to fair trial and due process
documents.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
documents.punishment: Any judicial or administrative order passed in violation of due process is unconstitutional, void ab initio, and nullity in the eyes of law.
documents.summary_plain: Guarantees every citizen the absolute fundamental right to a fair trial and due process of law in the determination of civil rights and obligations or in any criminal charge.
documents.summary_urdu: منصفانہ سماعت اور قانونی تقاضوں کی پابندی کا بنیادی حق (آرٹیکل 10-A)۔ ہر شہری کو صفائی کا موقع دیے بغیر یا جانبداری سے کیا گیا کوئی بھی فیصلہ غیر آئینی اور باطل ہوگا۔
documents.statutory_text: For the determination of his civil rights and obligations or in any criminal charge against him a person shall be entitled to a fair trial and due process.
evidence_required: Proof of denial of hearing (e.g. ex-parte order passed without serving summons)
Proof of bias or conflict of interest of the adjudicator
Violation of natural justice principles (Audi Alteram Partem - no one should be condemned unheard)
practical_steps: Invoke Article 10A in any appeal, revision, or writ petition where government or trial court violated natural justice.
Highlight lack of proper notice, denial of cross-examination, or denial of opportunity to present defense.
Seek setting aside of impugned order and remand for de novo fair hearing.

documents.act_title: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan (1973)
documents.section_title: Security of person and safeguards as to arrest and detention
documents.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
documents.punishment: Unlawful detention renders police officers liable for illegal confinement (Section 342 PPC) and departmental disciplinary action.
documents.summary_plain: Protects every person's life and liberty. No one can be deprived of liberty except in accordance with law. Anyone arrested must be informed immediately of the grounds of arrest, has the right to consult and be defended by a lawyer of their choice, and must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours.
documents.summary_urdu: شخصی آزادی اور گرفتاری کے خلاف بنیادی تحفظات (آرٹیکل 9 اور 10)۔ گرفتاری کی وجوہات سے آگاہ کرنا، وکیل سے مشاورت کا حق، اور 24 گھنٹے کے اندر مجسٹریٹ کے سامنے پیش کرنا لازمی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Article 9: No person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law. Article 10(1): No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest, nor shall he be denied the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice. Article 10(2): Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before a Magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest...
evidence_required: Police Daily Diary (Roznamcha) record or lockup register
Witness testimony of relatives present during unannounced arrest/abduction
Proof of detention exceeding 24 hours without remand order from Magistrate
practical_steps: If someone is detained without formal arrest record, immediately send telegrams/urgent notices to Sessions Judge and High Court Chief Justice.
File Habeas Corpus petition under Section 491 CrPC in High Court or Sessions Court.
Court appoints a Court Bailiff to raid police station, inspect lockup registers, and produce detainee before the Judge.
If detention was without lawful warrant, detainee is discharged immediately.

documents.act_title: Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act 1997 & NEPRA Regulations
documents.section_title: Redressal of electricity billing complaints, excessive billing, and WAPDA/DISCO disputes
documents.chapter: Consumer Protection and Complaint Handling
documents.jurisdiction: Federal (Applicable across all DISCOs: LESCO, IESCO, K-Electric, GEPCO, FESCO, MEPCO, PESCO, HESCO, QESCO)
documents.punishment: Rectification of inflated bill, cancellation of illegal detection bill, restoration of electricity supply, and compensation.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 39 of the NEPRA Act 1997 and the NEPRA Consumer Service Manual, any electricity consumer facing inflated or excessive electricity bills, arbitrary detection bills, defective meter reading, or tariff overbilling by distribution companies (DISCOs/WAPDA/IESCO/LESCO/KE) can file a formal complaint. The consumer can challenge the inflated bill before: (1) The Customer Services Center of the concerned DISCO; (2) The Provincial Electric Inspector under Section 26(6) of the Electricity Act 1910; (3) The NEPRA Consumer Affairs Division; or (4) The District Consumer Court under provincial Consumer Protection Acts. A consumer is entitled to stay of disconnection while a genuine billing dispute is under adjudication.
documents.summary_urdu: واپڈا اور بجلی کے زائد بلوں کے خلاف شکایت (نیپرا ایکٹ دفعہ 39 و کنزیومر پروٹیکشن)۔ اگر دکان یا گھر کا بجلی کا بل بہت زیادہ آئے، غلط ریڈنگ ہو یا ناجائز ڈٹیکشن بل ڈالا جائے، تو ایس ڈی او، پروونشل الیکٹرک انسپکٹر، نیپرا کنزیومر افیئرز اور کنزیومر کورٹ میں چیلنج کیا جا سکتا ہے اور کنکشن کٹنے سے حکمِ امتناعی لیا جا سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 39: Any interested person, including an electric power consumer, may file a complaint with the Authority regarding any violation of this Act, rules, regulations, or terms of a licence. The Authority or designated officer shall investigate and pass appropriate orders, including rectification of incorrect billing, setting aside unjustified detection bills, and compensation.
evidence_required: Copies of disputed electricity bills showing excessive units or detection charges
Previous 12 months electricity bills showing normal consumption pattern
Photographs of current electricity meter reading display showing discrepancy
Written complaint submitted to SDO/XEN with courier receipt or diary number
practical_steps: Take a clear timestamped photograph of the electric meter display to verify actual meter reading against the units billed.
Submit a written complaint to the local Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) or XEN of the electric distribution company demanding billing correction.
If DISCO fails to rectify within 15 days, lodge an online or physical complaint before the NEPRA Consumer Affairs Division (CAD).
Simultaneously apply to the Provincial Electric Inspector under Section 26(6) of Electricity Act 1910 for testing of meter and stay of disconnection.
Alternatively, file a consumer complaint before the District Consumer Protection Court seeking damages and cancellation of arbitrary billing.

documents.act_title: Punjab Consumer Protection Act (Act II of 2005)
documents.section_title: Liability for Defective Products, Faulty Goods, and Consumer Court Redressal
documents.chapter: Part II: Liability Arising from Defective Products and Part IV: Redress of Grievance
documents.jurisdiction: Provincial (Punjab Consumer Courts: Lahore, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, Multan, Gujranwala, Sialkot)
documents.punishment: Order for return of purchase price (refund), replacement of defective product, compensation, and penalty fine up to Rs. 50,000.
documents.summary_plain: Under Sections 4, 13, and 15 of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act 2005, a manufacturer or seller is strictly liable for selling defective goods, broken products, or items not conforming to standard or warranty. Before filing a claim in the District Consumer Court, the buyer MUST send a formal written 15-day legal notice under Section 28(1) demanding repair, replacement, or refund. If the seller or shopkeeper fails or refuses to resolve the dispute within 15 days of receiving the notice, the consumer must file a claim before the District Consumer Court within 30 days from the cause of action. The Consumer Court can order a full refund, product replacement, and damages for financial loss and mental distress.
documents.summary_urdu: ناقص یا خراب اشیاء کے خلاف صارف عدالت (پنجاب کنزیومر پروٹیکشن ایکٹ 2005 دفعہ 4، 13، 15 و 28)۔ اگر خریدا گیا لیپ ٹاپ، موبائل یا سامان خراب نکلے اور دکاندار وارنٹی، مرمت یا رقم واپسی سے انکار کرے، تو پہلے 15 دن کا قانونی نوٹس بھیجا جاتا ہے۔ اس کے بعد ڈسٹرکٹ کنزیومر کورٹ میں دعویٰ دائر کر کے رقم واپسی، سامان کی تبدیلی اور ہرجانہ طلب کیا جا سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 4: The manufacturer or seller shall be liable to a consumer for damages caused by the characteristic of the product that renders the product defective. Section 13: A product is defective if it does not conform to the standard, specification, or warranty. Section 15: The seller is liable if he fails to repair or replace the defective product within a reasonable time. Section 28: A consumer who has suffered damage, or was delivered defective product, may submit a claim to the Consumer Court after serving a fifteen days written notice to the manufacturer or provider.
evidence_required: Original purchase receipt, invoice, or payment slip showing seller details and date
Warranty card or guarantee certificate if provided
Written 15-day legal notice sent to the shopkeeper/manufacturer via registered post or courier
Courier tracking receipt and delivery confirmation slip of the 15-day notice
Photographs or technical expert inspection report documenting the defect
practical_steps: Preserve the original purchase invoice, retail receipt, and warranty card.
Draft and serve a formal 15-day written legal notice under Section 28(1) PCPA to the shopkeeper demanding refund, repair, or replacement.
Send the legal notice via UMS / TCS registered courier with delivery acknowledgment.
If the shopkeeper does not reply or refund within 15 days, prepare a Consumer Claim with affidavit.
File the claim before the District Consumer Court within 30 days of the date of cause of action (no court fee required).

documents.act_title: Contract Act (Act IX of 1872)
documents.section_title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
documents.chapter: Chapter VI: Of the Consequences of Breach of Contract
documents.punishment: Decree for compensation, general damages, and restitution of benefits.
documents.summary_plain: When a contract is broken, the injured party is entitled to receive compensation from the defaulting party for any direct loss or damage that naturally arose in the usual course of things, or which both parties knew would likely result from the breach. Speculative or remote damages are not granted.
documents.summary_urdu: معاہدے کی خلاف ورزی پر ہرجانے / نقصان کا دعویٰ (دفعات 73 اور 74)۔ جب کوئی فریق طے شدہ معاہدے سے پھر جائے تو متاثرہ فریق اس کی وجہ سے ہونے والے حقیقی مالی نقصان کا دعویٰ سول کورٹ میں کر سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 73: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it. Such compensation is not to be given for any remote and indirect loss or damage sustained by reason of the breach.
evidence_required: Original signed agreement / contract with terms clearly defining obligations and deadlines
Notice of breach dispatched to defaulting party with TCS / courier receipts
Documentary proof of actual financial loss incurred (invoices, replacement purchase receipts, ledger entries, bank debits)
Proof that plaintiff was ready and willing to perform their own side of the contract
practical_steps: Issue a formal Legal Notice through an Advocate pointing out specific contractual defaults and calling upon the party to perform within 15 days.
Calculate actual liquidated and direct losses substantiated by receipts.
File a Civil Suit for Recovery of Damages and Breach of Contract before the competent Civil Court.
Seek attachment before judgment under Order XXXVIII Rule 5 CPC if defendant is attempting to siphon off assets.

documents.section_title: Rejection of Plaint
documents.chapter: First Schedule: Order VII - Plaint
documents.punishment: Dismissal of a frivolous, barred, or non-maintainable suit at the threshold.
documents.summary_plain: Empowers the defendant to request dismissal of the plaintiff's lawsuit right at the start without having to undergo a lengthy trial, if the plaint discloses no real cause of action, is barred by limitation/statute, or is improperly valued.
documents.summary_urdu: دعویٰ خارج کرنے کی درخواست (ریجیکشن آف پلینٹ)۔ جب مخالف فریق کا مقدمہ بلا جواز، قانون کی رو سے ممنوع یا میعاد گزرنے کے بعد دائر کیا گیا ہو تو اسے شروع میں ہی خارج کروایا جا سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: The plaint shall be rejected in the following cases: (a) where it does not disclose a cause of action; (b) where the relief claimed is undervalued, and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to correct the valuation within a time to be fixed by the Court, fails to do so; (c) where the relief claimed is properly valued, but the plaint is written upon paper insufficiently stamped; (d) where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law.
evidence_required: Application under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC highlighting defects in the plaintiff's plaint
Statutory bar evidence (e.g. Limitation Act schedule, bar under specific tenancy/arbitration law)
Proof that no legal cause of action is disclosed on the face of the plaint
practical_steps: Before filing a full written statement, file an application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC.
Pinpoint legal defects: limitation expiry, lack of cause of action, or lack of court jurisdiction.
If the court agrees, the plaint is rejected and the litigation ends without full evidence trial.

documents.section_title: Revision jurisdiction
documents.chapter: Part VIII: Reference, Review and Revision
documents.punishment: Correction of jurisdictional error, illegality, or material irregularity committed by subordinate court.
documents.summary_plain: Provides a remedy before the High Court (or District Court) against non-appealable orders of subordinate civil courts where the subordinate judge exercised jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise jurisdiction, or acted with material irregularity.
documents.summary_urdu: نگرانی (ریویژن)۔ ماتحت عدالت کے غیر قانونی حکم یا دائرہ اختیار سے تجاوز کے خلاف ہائی کورٹ یا ڈسٹرکٹ کورٹ میں دائر کی جانے والی درخواست۔
documents.statutory_text: The High Court may call for the record of any case which has been decided by any Court subordinate to such High Court and in which no appeal lies thereto, and if such subordinate Court appears: (a) to have exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it by law, or (b) to have failed to exercise a jurisdiction so vested, or (c) to have acted in the exercise of its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity, the High Court may make such order in the case as it thinks fit.
evidence_required: Certified copies of the impugned order and subordinate court record
Grounds of Revision demonstrating jurisdictional defect or illegality
Affidavit and power of attorney (Wakalatnama)
practical_steps: Obtain certified copies of the trial court's order within the limitation period (90 days).
Engage an Advocate of the High Court to draft Civil Revision petition.
File petition in High Court Civil Registry; argue admission and seek suspension of impugned order.

documents.section_title: Execution of Decrees and Orders (Recovery of decretal amount and property possession)
documents.chapter: Part II (Execution) and First Schedule: Order XXI
documents.punishment: Enforcement of decree by attachment and sale of debtor's property, attachment of bank accounts, and arrest/detention in civil prison.
documents.summary_plain: When a litigant wins a civil court case and obtains a final decree, but the opposing party (judgment-debtor) fails or refuses to pay the decree amount or hand over property, the decree-holder must NOT file a fresh suit. Instead, they must file an Execution Petition under Order XXI of the CPC before the executing court. The court has coercive statutory powers to enforce satisfaction through: (a) attachment and auction sale of the debtor's properties; (b) attachment of bank accounts; and (c) arrest and civil jail detention of the debtor under Order 21 Rule 37/38. Under Section 48 CPC, limitation for fresh execution applications is up to 6 years.
documents.summary_urdu: ڈگری کا اجراء (ایگزیکیوشن آف ڈگری - آرڈر 21 و دفعہ 48 ضابطہ دیوانی)۔ جب عدالت سے کیس جیت جانے کے بعد مخالف فریق ڈگری کی رقم ادا نہ کرے، تو نیا مقدمہ دائر نہیں کیا جاتا بلکہ اسی عدالت میں 'درخواستِ اجراء' دائر کی جاتی ہے۔ عدالت مقروض کے بینک اکاؤنٹس، جائیداد قرق اور نیلام کروا سکتی ہے اور گرفتاری کا وارنٹ جاری کرتی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 38: A decree may be executed either by the Court which passed it, or by the Court to which it is sent for execution. Order XXI Rule 10: Where the holder of a decree desires to execute it, he shall apply to the Court which passed the decree. Section 51: Subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed, the Court may, on the application of the decree-holder, order execution of the decree: (a) by delivery of any property specifically decreed; (b) by attachment and sale or by sale without attachment of any property; (c) by arrest and detention in prison; (d) by appointing a receiver. Section 48: Execution barred in certain cases after six years.
evidence_required: Certified copy of the judgment and decree sheet
Calculation memo of outstanding decretal amount including statutory markup
List and schedule of judgment-debtor's assets, bank accounts, or immovable properties
Certificate of non-satisfaction from the trial court
practical_steps: Obtain certified copy of the decree sheet from the copying branch.
Calculate the limitation period (first execution within 3 years under Article 182 Limitation Act, subject to Section 48 CPC maximum 6 years).
File Execution Application under Order XXI Rule 10 & 11 CPC before the executing court.
File an application for attachment of judgment-debtor's bank accounts, vehicles, and immovable property under Order XXI Rule 43 and Rule 54 CPC.
If the judgment-debtor evades payment, apply for arrest warrant and detention in civil prison under Order XXI Rules 37 & 38 CPC.

documents.act_title: Code of Civil Procedure (Act V of 1908)
documents.section_title: Court Summons, Inspection of Case Plaint, and Written Statement
documents.chapter: First Schedule: Order V & Order VIII
documents.punishment: Failure to appear may result in ex-parte proceedings and an ex-parte decree under Order IX Rule 6 CPC.
documents.summary_plain: When a person receives a court notice or summons (such as giving 7 or 14 days to respond) without knowing what the case is about, they must NOT ignore it. The recipient or their appointed advocate must appear before the court on the scheduled hearing date, inspect the court file, and obtain a certified copy of the plaint (daawa) and annexed documents from the copying branch. Under Order VIII Rule 1 CPC, the defendant is entitled to request time (ordinarily 30 days) to submit a formal Written Statement (jawab-e-daawa) contesting the suit.
documents.summary_urdu: عدالتی سمن یا نوٹس ملنے پر قانونی طریقہ کار (آرڈر 5 و آرڈر 8 ضابطہ دیوانی)۔ جب عدالت سے نوٹس موصول ہو تو اسے نظر انداز نہ کریں ورنہ یکطرفہ کارروائی ہو سکتی ہے۔ مدعا علیہ یا ان کا وکیل مقررہ تاریخ پر عدالت میں پیش ہو کر دعوے اور نقول کا معائنہ کرے اور جواب دعویٰ داخل کرنے کے لیے وقت طلب کرے۔
documents.statutory_text: Order V Rule 1: When a suit has been duly instituted, a summons may be issued to the defendant to appear and answer the claim on a day to be therein specified. Order VIII Rule 1: The defendant may, and if so required by the Court shall, at or before the first hearing or within such time as the Court may permit, present a written statement of his defence.
evidence_required: Original court notice or summons received with envelope showing diary/suit number and court stamp
Power of Attorney (Wakalatnama) executed in favour of an enrolled Advocate
Certified copy of the plaint (daawa) and all annexures obtained from the court copying branch
Any defense documents, receipts, or agreements contradicting the plaintiff's claim
practical_steps: Examine the court notice to identify the specific court, judge, suit title, and the fixed hearing date.
Do not ignore the notice; failure to appear will cause the court to initiate ex-parte proceedings under Order IX Rule 6 CPC.
Engage an advocate to appear on the designated date and submit a Memo of Appearance or Wakalatnama.
Apply to the court reader or copying branch for an urgent copy of the plaint and all attached documents to understand the allegations.
Seek time under Order VIII Rule 1 CPC to file a formal Written Statement (jawab-e-daawa) addressing each paragraph of the plaint.

documents.chapter: Chapter II: Of the Constitution of Criminal Courts and Offices
documents.punishment: Judicial direction to police officers to register FIR, prevent police harassment, or transfer dishonest investigation.
documents.summary_plain: Provides a crucial legal remedy when local police refuse to register an FIR or harass citizens. The Sessions Judge or Additional Sessions Judge acts as Ex-Officio Justice of the Peace and can issue binding orders directing the SHO to register the FIR or act according to law.

Attach the stamped police complaint, supporting evidence, and affidavit.

documents.section_title: In what cases bail to be taken (Bailable offences)
documents.chapter: Chapter XXXIX: Of Bail
documents.cognizable: Applies when accused is arrested or appears before court
documents.punishment: Accused is entitled to bail as a matter of absolute legal right upon furnishing surety.
documents.summary_plain: For offences classified as 'bailable' under the CrPC Second Schedule, the grant of bail is an absolute statutory right. The police officer or magistrate cannot refuse bail once solvent surety or personal bond is furnished.
documents.summary_urdu: قابلِ ضمانت جرائم میں ضمانت۔ یہ ملزم کا بنیادی قانونی حق ہے۔ پولیس یا مجسٹریٹ مناسب مچلکہ / ضامن پیش کرنے پر ضمانت دینے سے انکار نہیں کر سکتے۔
documents.statutory_text: When any person other than a person accused of a non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station, or appears or is brought before a Court, and is prepared at any time while in the custody of such officer or at any stage of the proceedings before such Court to give bail, such person shall be released on bail.
evidence_required: Bail application with certified copy of FIR
Surety bonds (Zamanat nama) by solvent local surety with CNIC and property document / fard
Affidavit of surety
practical_steps: Obtain certified copy of FIR and remand paper.
File Bail Application under Section 496 CrPC before the Area Judicial Magistrate.
Produce local solvent surety with original CNIC and registry/fard of property.
Upon court satisfaction, Robkar (release order) is issued to the jail or investigating officer.

documents.section_title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence (Post-arrest bail)
documents.chapter: Chapter XXXIX: Of Bail
documents.cognizable: Applies after arrest in non-bailable cases
documents.punishment: Judicial discretion based on prohibitory clause, statutory delay, or case of further inquiry.
documents.summary_plain: Governs post-arrest bail in non-bailable offences. If the offence is not punishable with death, life imprisonment, or 10 years (non-prohibitory clause), bail is the rule and jail is an exception. Also provides statutory bail for women, minors, sick persons, or cases of unexplained delay.
documents.summary_urdu: بعد از گرفتاری ضمانت (پوسٹ اریسٹ بیل)۔ غیر قابلِ ضمانت جرائم میں سیشن یا ہائی کورٹ سے رہائی کے اصول، خاص طور پر خواتین، نابالغوں، بیمار افراد یا مزید تفتیش کے معاملات میں۔
documents.statutory_text: When any person accused of any non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant... he may be released on bail, but he shall not be so released if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years: Provided that the Court may direct that any person under the age of sixteen years or any woman or any sick or infirm person accused of such an offence be released on bail...
evidence_required: Certified copy of FIR and police investigation diary excerpts
Medical records if seeking bail on grounds of sickness or infirmity
Proof of minority (NADRA B-form / birth certificate) if under 16 years
Evidence indicating lack of specific role or false implication
practical_steps: File Bail Application under Section 497 CrPC before Judicial Magistrate or Sessions Judge.
Demonstrate that either the offence falls outside the prohibitory clause, or there are reasonable grounds for further inquiry under subsection (2).
If dismissed by Sessions Court, file Criminal Bail Application before the High Court.

documents.section_title: Power to direct admission to bail or reduction of bail (Pre-Arrest Bail / Bail Before Arrest)
documents.chapter: Chapter XXXIX: Of Bail
documents.category: Criminal Procedure / Protection Against Unlawful Arrest
documents.punishment: Protection from police arrest to prevent humiliation, harassment, or unjustified detention.
documents.summary_plain: Pre-arrest bail protects an innocent person against imminent arrest, humiliation, and malicious prosecution by police or political opponents. The petitioner must demonstrate ulterior motives, mala fides, or lack of credible evidence.
documents.summary_urdu: قبل از گرفتاری ضمانت (پری اریسٹ بیل)۔ پولیس کی ناجائز گرفتاری، ذلت اور بدنیتی سے بچاؤ کے لیے سیشن یا ہائی کورٹ سے حفاظتی ضمانت لینا۔
documents.statutory_text: The amount of every bond executed under this Chapter shall be fixed with due regard to the circumstances of the case, and shall not be excessive; and the High Court or Court of Session may, in any case, whether there be an appeal on conviction or not, direct that any person be admitted to bail, or that the bail required by a police officer or Magistrate be reduced.
evidence_required: Copy of FIR or proof of police raids / threat of arrest
Proof of mala fides / ulterior motives of complainant or police (past enmity, cross-complaints)
Applicant must appear in person before the Court
Affidavit affirming innocence and willingness to join police investigation
practical_steps: Petitioner must personally appear before the Sessions Court along with an Advocate.
File Pre-arrest Bail Application under Section 498 CrPC showing apprehension of arrest due to malice.
Court grants Ad-interim Pre-Arrest Bail and calls for police file.
Petitioner must join police investigation (Tafteesh) and mark presence.
On final date of hearing, Court confirms or recalls the pre-arrest bail.

documents.section_title: Procedure where dispute concerning land, water, or boundaries is likely to cause breach of peace
documents.chapter: Chapter XII: Disputes as to Immovable Property
documents.punishment: Attachment of property, sealing of premises, or order restoring actual possession.
documents.summary_plain: Used when a property dispute threatens public peace or armed conflict. The Executive Magistrate / Court can seal the disputed property or determine who had actual physical possession on the date of the order, preventing violent dispossession while civil title is decided in civil court.
documents.summary_urdu: اراضی یا جائیداد کے تنازعات سے امنِ عامہ میں خلل روکنے کی کارروائی۔ مجسٹریٹ جائیداد کو سربمہر (سیل) کر سکتا ہے یا موجودہ قابض کے حق میں امن قائم رکھنے کا حکم دے سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Whenever an Executive Magistrate is satisfied from a police-report or other information that a dispute likely to cause a breach of the peace exists concerning any land or water or the boundaries thereof... he shall make an order in writing, stating the grounds of his being so satisfied, and requiring the parties concerned in such dispute to attend his Court... and to put in written statements of their respective claims as respects the fact of actual possession of the subject of dispute.
evidence_required: Police report or complaint confirming likelihood of armed clash or breach of peace
Utility bills, rent agreements, or possession receipts proving actual physical possession
Photographs or videos of dispute or security threat
practical_steps: File an application under Section 145 CrPC before the Magistrate detailing threat of violence over property possession.
Magistrate issues preliminary order and calls for police report.
Magistrate may attach (seal) property pending inquiry if emergency exists.
Parties submit proof of possession; Magistrate restores or protects possession of party unlawfully evicted within 2 months.

documents.section_title: Appeal from sentence of Judicial Magistrate or Court of Session
documents.chapter: Chapter XXXI: Of Appeals
documents.bailable: Bail pending appeal under Section 426 CrPC
documents.punishment: Power of Appellate Court to reverse conviction, acquit the accused, reduce sentence, or order a retrial.
documents.summary_plain: Under Sections 408 and 410 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an accused person convicted by a lower court (such as a Judicial Magistrate or Sessions Judge) has an absolute statutory right of criminal appeal. The trial court's decision is not final. The appellate court re-examines both factual findings and legal evidence, can suspend the sentence and grant bail pending appeal under Section 426 CrPC, and will overturn an improper conviction to acquit the appellant if reasonable doubt exists.
documents.summary_urdu: ماتحت عدالت کی سزا کے خلاف اپیل کا حق (دفعات 408 اور 410)۔ مجسٹریٹ یا سیشن جج کی طرف سے سنائی گئی سزا کے خلاف ہر شہری کو سیشن کورٹ یا ہائی کورٹ میں اپیل دائر کرنے کا قانونی حق حاصل ہے۔ اپیل کے دوران دفعہ 426 کے تحت سزا معطل کروا کر ضمانت بھی حاصل کی جا سکتی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 408: Any person convicted on a trial held by an Assistant Sessions Judge, a District Magistrate or other Magistrate of the first class... may appeal to the Court of Session. Section 410: Any person convicted on a trial held by a Sessions Judge, or an Additional Sessions Judge, may appeal to the High Court.
evidence_required: Certified copy of trial court judgment and conviction order
Certified copies of oral depositions and testimonies of prosecution witnesses (PWs)
Certified copies of exhibited documents and defense evidence
Memo of Appeal detailing grounds of challenge and misappreciation of evidence
practical_steps: Obtain certified copies of the conviction judgment and trial court record immediately.
File Criminal Appeal within statutory limitation period (30 days to Sessions Court, 60 days to High Court).
File an application under Section 426 CrPC for suspension of sentence and release on bail pending final disposal of the appeal.
Argue grounds showing that the prosecution failed to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt or relied on flawed, uncorroborated testimony.

documents.section_title: Pre-trial reconciliation and Decree of Khula
documents.chapter: Pre-trial Proceedings
documents.punishment: Judicial dissolution of Muslim marriage on ground of Khula.
documents.summary_plain: Under Pakistani law, a Muslim wife has an absolute legal and Islamic right to obtain Khula if she cannot live with her husband within the limits ordained by Allah. If pre-trial reconciliation fails and the wife refuses to reconcile, the Family Court is legally bound to grant a decree for dissolution of marriage immediately, subject to returning 25% to 50% of the prompt dower (or surrendering unpaid dower).

evidence_required: Plaint stating clear, unequivocal aversion and inability to live with the husband within Islamic limits
Copy of Nikahnama showing dower details (prompt / deferred / paid / unpaid)
Statement of the wife before the Family Judge during pre-trial reconciliation affirming firm decision
practical_steps: File suit for Dissolution of Marriage on grounds of Khula before the Family Court.
Attend the pre-trial reconciliation hearing before the Judge.
If the wife stands firm that reconciliation is impossible, the Court passes a preliminary Khula decree.
The Family Court transmits a copy of the decree to the relevant Union Council Chairman for 90-day statutory notice under Section 7 MFLO.

documents.act_title: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance (Ordinance VIII of 1961)
documents.section_title: Talaq (Divorce) procedure and notice to Union Council
documents.chapter: Divorce Proceedings and Effectiveness
documents.jurisdiction: Federal (Applicable to all Muslim citizens of Pakistan)
documents.cognizable: Non-cognizable / Quasi-penal for failure to notify
documents.punishment: Failure to deliver notice to Chairman is punishable with simple imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to 5,000 rupees.
documents.summary_plain: Any husband pronouncing Talaq must immediately give written notice to the Chairman of the local Union Council / Arbitration Council and provide a copy to the wife. Talaq does not become legally effective until 90 days have expired from the date the notice was delivered to the Chairman, during which the Arbitration Council must attempt reconciliation.
documents.summary_urdu: طلاق کا قانونی طریقہ کار اور یونین کونسل نوٹس۔ طلاق دینے کے بعد چیئرمین یونین کونسل کو تحریری نوٹس دینا لازمی ہے۔ 90 دن کی عدت/مفاہمتی مدت پوری ہونے کے بعد طلاق کا موثر سرٹیفکیٹ جاری ہوتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Any man who wishes to divorce his wife shall, as soon as may be after the pronouncement of Talaq in any form whatsoever, give the Chairman notice in writing of his having done so, and shall supply a copy thereof to the wife... Save as provided in subsection (5), a Talaq, unless revoked earlier, expressly or otherwise, shall not be effective until the expiration of ninety days from the day on which notice under subsection (1) is delivered to the Chairman.
evidence_required: Written Talaq-Nama signed by husband and attested by witnesses
TCS/Postal registry receipt of notice dispatched to the Union Council Chairman and to the wife
Attested receiving stamp from the Union Council / Arbitration Council
practical_steps: Execute written Talaq-nama with two male Muslim witnesses.
Send formal statutory notice to the Chairman Union Council where the marriage took place or where the wife resides, along with a copy to the wife via registered mail.
Participate in the 3 reconciliation sessions convened by the Arbitration Council.
Upon completion of 90 days without revocation, obtain the official 'Divorce Effectiveness Certificate' (Talaq Certificate) from the Union Council/NADRA.

documents.section_title: Maintenance of wife and minor children
documents.chapter: Maintenance Rights
documents.cognizable: Family Remedy / Executable as land revenue arrears
documents.punishment: Non-payment results in attachment of bank accounts, salary deduction, property auction, or civil imprisonment.
documents.summary_plain: A Muslim husband and father is under an absolute legal and religious obligation to maintain his wife during the subsistence of marriage (and during iddat) and his minor children (sons until adulthood, daughters until marriage). If he fails, the Family Court awards monthly maintenance and past maintenance arrears.
documents.summary_urdu: بیوی اور بچوں کا ماہانہ خرچہ (نان و نفقہ)۔ باپ اور شوہر پر قانونی فرض ہے کہ وہ بیوی اور بچوں کا مناسب خوراک، رہائش، تعلیم اور علاج کا خرچ ادا کرے۔ عدم ادائیگی پر قید ہو سکتی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: If any husband fails to maintain his wife adequately, or where there are more wives than one, fails to maintain them equitably, the wife, or all or any of the wives, may in addition to seeking any other legal remedy available apply to the Chairman who shall constitute an Arbitration Council to determine the matter... Family Courts also hold jurisdiction under Family Courts Act 1964 Section 5 to award interim and final maintenance.
evidence_required: Proof of marriage and birth certificates / NADRA B-Form of children
Documented monthly expenses of children (school tuition fee receipts, medical bills, utility bills)
Proof of father's financial capacity (company salary slip, income tax returns, vehicle registration, business accounts, lifestyle proof)
practical_steps: File suit for recovery of past and future monthly maintenance before the Family Court.
File an application for Interim Maintenance (Section 17-A Family Courts Act) to obtain urgent monthly support pending trial.
If the husband defaults in paying court-fixed maintenance, the Court strikes off his defense and issues arrest warrants / execution decree under Order XXI CPC.

documents.section_title: Appointment of guardian and custody of minors (Welfare of the Minor)
documents.chapter: Appointment and Custody
documents.punishment: Court determines physical custody and weekly/monthly visitation schedule based exclusively on the child's welfare.
documents.summary_plain: The paramount and supreme consideration in custody disputes under Pakistani law is the 'Welfare of the Minor' (health, education, moral upbringing, emotional bond). While mothers traditionally have custody (Hizanat) during tender years, the court evaluates what best serves the child's long-term future, while granting the non-custodial parent regular visitation rights.
documents.summary_urdu: بچوں کی کسٹڈی (حضانت) اور والدین سے ملاقات۔ کسٹڈی کا فیصلہ کرتے وقت عدالت کا واحد اور بنیادی معیار 'بچے کی بہترین فلاح و بہبود' ہوتا ہے۔ غیر نگران والد/والدہ کو عدالتی ملاقات کے حقوق حاصل ہوتے ہیں۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 17: In appointing or declaring the guardian of a minor, the Court shall, subject to the provisions of this section, be guided by what, consistently with the law to which the minor is subject, appears in the circumstances to be for the welfare of the minor. Section 25: Title of guardian to custody of ward.
evidence_required: School report cards, medical records, and daily living environment proof
Character and financial stability proof of the custodial claimant
Age and personal preference of minor (if capable of forming intelligent preference)
Proof of neglect, abuse, or alienation by either parent (if alleged)
practical_steps: File petition for custody under Section 25 Guardian and Wards Act read with Section 5 Family Courts Act.
File urgent interim custody application or visitation application to meet the child at least twice a month or weekly.
Guardian Judge meets the child in chamber to ascertain preference if of sufficient discernment.
Final decree establishes custody along with a comprehensive visitation schedule (weekends, Eid holidays, summer vacations).

documents.act_title: Family Courts Act (Act XXXV of 1964) & Dowry Laws
documents.section_title: Recovery of dowry articles, bridal gifts, and personal jewelry (Saman-e-Jahez & Zewar)
documents.chapter: Exclusive Jurisdiction of Family Courts
documents.punishment: Decree directing return of specific gold jewelry and dowry items or payment of current market value; enforceable through arrest and property attachment.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 5 read with the First Schedule (Entry 7) of the Family Courts Act 1964 and dowry legislation, bridal jewelry (gold/zewar), clothes, and dowry articles (Saman-e-Jahez) are the absolute personal property of the woman. If her husband, father-in-law, or in-laws withhold or refuse to return her jewelry or dowry items, she has the legal right to file a Suit for Recovery of Dowry Articles or the alternate market value thereof before the Family Court. Misappropriation of entrusted jewelry also constitutes criminal breach of trust.
documents.summary_urdu: سامانِ جہیز اور زیورات کی واپسی (فیملی کورٹس ایکٹ دفعہ 5)۔ شادی پر دیے گئے سونے کے زیورات اور سامانِ جہیز بیوی کی ذاتی ملکیت ہیں۔ اگر شوہر یا سسر زیور واپس کرنے سے انکار کریں تو فیملی کورٹ سے زیورات یا ان کی موجودہ مارکیٹ قیمت کی وصولی کا دعویٰ دائر کیا جاتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Family Courts Act 1964, Section 5 & Schedule Entry 7: The Family Courts shall have exclusive jurisdiction to entertain, hear and adjudicate upon matters specified in the Schedule, including: Entry 7: Dowry and bridal gifts or the alternate value thereof. Under Dowry and Bridal Gifts (Restriction) Act 1976 Section 3, all property given as bridal gifts or dowry vests absolutely in the bride.
evidence_required: Itemized list of dowry articles and bridal jewelry prepared at the time of marriage (signed or witnessed)
Original goldsmith purchase receipts or valuation certificates
Photographs or wedding video showing bride wearing the jewelry at Rukhsati
Entries in Nikahnama regarding bridal gifts and jewelry (Columns 16-17)
practical_steps: Prepare an itemized list of all gold jewelry, bridal gifts, and dowry articles with estimated current market value.
Engage an Advocate to file a Plaint for Recovery of Dowry Articles or Alternate Market Value under Section 5 Family Courts Act.
File an application for preservation and deposit of jewelry if danger of sale/misappropriation exists.
Execute decree through Family Court powers under Section 13 Family Courts Act (attachment of property or detention in civil jail).

documents.summary_plain: Under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act 1936, where an employer has delayed, withheld, or refused to pay monthly wages/salary, or made unauthorized deductions, the employee can file a recovery claim before the Authority appointed under the Payment of Wages Act (Labour Court / Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation). The Authority has statutory powers to direct immediate payment of all unpaid salary arrears along with punitive compensation. If the employer still refuses to pay, the amount is recovered as arrears of land revenue by the District Collector.

documents.statutory_text: Section 15: The Provincial Government may appoint an Authority to hear and decide all claims arising out of deductions from the wages, or delay in payment of the wages, of persons employed or paid in that area. The Authority may direct the refund to the employed person of the amount deducted, or the payment of the delayed wages, together with the payment of such compensation as the Authority may think fit, not exceeding ten times the amount deducted.
evidence_required: Appointment letter, employment contract, or employee ID card
Bank statements showing past salary credits and subsequent non-payment
Attendance register records, emails, or WhatsApp messages confirming performance of duties
Written grievance notice or demand letter delivered to the employer
practical_steps: Serve a formal written demand notice on the employer demanding release of unpaid salary arrears within 7 days.
Calculate limitation period from the date wages fell into arrears.
Engage an Advocate or Labour Representative to file an Application under Section 15 Payment of Wages Act before the Authority.
Request the Authority to summon employer records and attendance/payroll registers.
Upon order, execute recovery through the District Collector as arrears of land revenue.

documents.act_title: Limitation Act (Act IX of 1908)
documents.section_title: Statutory limitation periods, effect of fraud, and dismissal of time-barred claims
documents.chapter: Part II: Limitation of Suits, Appeals and Applications
documents.jurisdiction: Federal / Provincial (Applied across all Pakistani Civil Courts)
documents.punishment: Mandatory dismissal of time-barred suits and applications under Section 3 Limitation Act.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 3 of the Limitation Act 1908, every lawsuit filed after the expiry of the prescribed limitation period must be dismissed by the civil court, even if the opposing party does not raise the objection. For immovable property and inheritance claims, the general limitation for possession is 12 years (Articles 142/144), 6 years for declaration of rights (Article 120), and 3 years for setting aside fraudulent transfers (Article 95). However, under Section 18 of the Limitation Act, if a party has been kept from knowledge of their right or fraudulent transaction through fraud, limitation begins only from the date when the fraud was first discovered.
documents.summary_urdu: قانونِ میعاد سماعت (لمیٹیشن ایکٹ 1908 - دفعات 3 اور 18)۔ اگر کوئی مقدمہ قانونی میعاد گزرنے کے بعد دائر کیا جائے تو عدالت اسے لازمی خارج کر دیتی ہے۔ تاہم دفعہ 18 کے تحت اگر مخالف فریق نے دھوکہ دہی سے وراثت یا جائیداد کا انتقال خفیہ رکھا ہو، تو میعاد کا شمار اس دن سے ہوتا ہے جس دن فراڈ کا علم ہوا۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 3: Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 25 (inclusive), every suit instituted, appeal preferred, and application made, after the period of limitation prescribed therefor by the first schedule shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence. Section 18: Where any person having a right to institute a suit or make an application has, by means of fraud, been kept from the knowledge of such right or of the title on which it is founded... the time limited for instituting a suit or making an application against the person guilty of the fraud or accessory thereto... shall be computed from the time when the fraud first became known to the person injuriously affected thereby.
evidence_required: Exact date of cause of action and date when fraud was first discovered
Documentary proof establishing active concealment of the fraudulent transfer
Revenue mutation or registry record showing date of unauthorized transfer
NADRA Family Registration Certificate establishing status as legal heir
practical_steps: Evaluate whether the claim falls within the 6-year or 12-year statutory period under the First Schedule of Limitation Act 1908.

If filing after a long delay (such as 10 or 12 years), specifically plead Section 18 of the Limitation Act in the plaint, demonstrating that the fraudulent mutation was concealed and discovered recently.
Anticipate and prepare counter-arguments against the defendant's preliminary objection under Order VII Rule 11 CPC regarding limitation.
File Suit for Declaration (Section 42 Specific Relief Act) and cancellation of fraudulent mutation with express prayer on limitation discovery.

documents.act_title: Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance (Ordinance XIX of 1965)
documents.section_title: Power to detain vehicle used without certificate of registration or permit (Impoundment)
documents.chapter: Chapter IX: Offences, Penalties and Procedure
documents.category: Traffic & Motor Vehicle Law / Regulatory Offence
documents.bailable: Bailable on verification of genuine documentation and fine clearance
documents.compoundable: Compoundable by payment of prescribed challan / fine or Magistrate release order
documents.punishment: Detention and impounding of the motor vehicle in traffic police custody or impound yard until ownership, valid registration, and authorized number plates are formally verified.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 115 of the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1965, any police officer in uniform or authorized transport authority has the statutory power to seize, detain, and impound any motor vehicle (car, motorcycle, commercial vehicle) if it is being driven without a valid certificate of registration, with mismatched, fake, or non-standard number plates, or without a valid permit. The vehicle remains impounded at the traffic police station or impound lot until genuine ownership and registration documents are verified and relevant challan fines are cleared.
documents.summary_urdu: موٹر وہیکل آرڈیننس 1965 کی دفعہ 115 کے تحت پولیس یا ٹریفک وارڈن کو غیر رجسٹرڈ گاڑی، بغیر نمبر پلیٹ، یا غلط/غیر مماثل نمبر پلیٹ والی کار یا موٹر سائیکل کو موقع پر ضبط اور بند (امپاؤنڈ) کرنے کا قانونی اختیار ہے۔ قانونی دستاویزات کی جانچ اور چالان کلیئرنس کے بعد گاڑی واپس لی جا سکتی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 115: Any police officer authorized in this behalf or other person authorized in this behalf by the Provincial Government may, if he has reason to believe that a motor vehicle has been or is being used in contravention of the provisions of section 22, section 23, or section 39 or without the permit required by sub-section (1) of section 44, seize and detain the vehicle, and for this purpose take or cause to be taken any steps he may consider necessary for the temporary safe custody of the vehicle.
evidence_required: Original Vehicle Registration Book or Smart Card issued by Excise and Taxation Department
Valid Computerized National Identity Card (CNIC) of registered owner
Official Traffic Police Impound Chit / Seizure Memo (Zabti Parwana / Challan)
Standard government-issued computerized registration plates matching engine and chassis numbers
Biometric transfer receipt or sale deed with authority letter if vehicle was recently purchased
Valid Driving Licence of the driver
practical_steps: Obtain the official Traffic Challan and Impound Receipt from the impounding officer showing the reason for detention and impound pound location.
Gather the original Excise Registration Smart Card/Book, valid CNIC, and proof of authorized computerized number plates.
If the number plate was mismatched due to registration delay or transfer, obtain a verification certificate from the Excise & Taxation Department.
Present the original registration documents and proof of payment of any fine to the Traffic Sector Incharge or designated Judicial Magistrate (Traffic).
Obtain formal release order (Robkar / Superdari under Section 115 PMVO / Section 516-A CrPC) and retrieve the vehicle from the impound lot.

documents.section_title: Necessity for registration and display of registration marks (Number Plates)
documents.chapter: Chapter III: Registration of Motor Vehicles
documents.category: Traffic & Motor Vehicle Law / Regulatory Offence
documents.compoundable: Compoundable via challan fine and plate regularization
documents.punishment: Fine under Section 112 and detention of vehicle under Section 115 until lawful display of authorized number plates.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 23 of the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1965, no person is permitted to drive any motor vehicle, and no owner may allow a vehicle to be driven in any public place, unless the vehicle is duly registered and displays the official registration mark and prescribed computerized number plates. Driving with unregistered vehicles, non-matching plates, fancy plates, or obscured plates violates Section 23 and empowers traffic police to issue challans and impound the vehicle.
documents.summary_urdu: دفعہ 23 کے تحت بغیر رجسٹریشن یا بغیر مجاز کمپیوٹرائزڈ نمبر پلیٹ کے کوئی بھی موٹر گاڑی یا موٹر سائیکل چلانا ممنوع ہے۔ غیر مماثل یا فینسی نمبر پلیٹ پر چالان اور دفعہ 115 کے تحت گاڑی بند ہو سکتی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 23: No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place or in any other place for the purpose of carrying passengers or goods, unless the vehicle is registered in accordance with this Chapter and the vehicle carries a registration mark displayed in the prescribed manner.
evidence_required: Excise Registration Certificate showing assigned registration mark
Official excise-issued computerized number plates
Excise tax payment receipts
practical_steps: Apply immediately to the Motor Registration Authority for issuance of official computerized number plates.
Keep the official excise receipt and original registration card in the vehicle while awaiting original plates.
Replace any non-standard or temporary plate with authorized government plates to avoid seizure under Section 115.

documents.section_title: Offences against dignity of natural person and cyber-stalking / blackmailing
documents.chapter: Chapter II: Offences and Penalties
documents.cognizable: Cognizable by FIA Cyber Crime Wing
documents.bailable: Bailable / Non-bailable depending on whether child or non-consensual sexually explicit content is involved
documents.punishment: Section 20: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 1 million rupees or both. Section 21 (Cyber-stalking / sharing intimate pictures): Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 1 million rupees, and up to 5 years if victim is a minor.
documents.summary_plain: Protects individuals from online defamation, blackmailing, harassment on WhatsApp/Facebook/Instagram, cyber-stalking, morphing photos, and non-consensual sharing of private pictures or videos.
documents.summary_urdu: سائبر کرائم، آن لائن بلیک میلنگ اور ہراسانی (دفعات 20 اور 21)۔ سوشل میڈیا یا واٹس ایپ پر تصاویر وائرل کرنے کی دھمکی، نازیبا پیغامات، جعلی اکاؤنٹس اور بلیک میلنگ کے خلاف ایف آئی اے سائبر کرائم کا سخت ایکشن۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 20: Whoever intentionally and publicly exhibits or displays or transmits any information through any information system, which he knows to be false, and intimidates or harms the reputation or privacy of a natural person, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years or with fine. Section 21: A person commits cyber-stalking if with intent to coerce or intimidate or harass any person, he uses information system or electronic device to follow, contact, spy on, or distribute pictures/videos without consent.
evidence_required: Screenshots of harassing messages, profiles, phone numbers, or social media links (URL)
Uncompressed exported chat logs (.txt) and media files
Details of extortion demands (bank accounts, easy paisa / jazz cash accounts requested)
Digital device with original messages intact for FIA forensic extraction
practical_steps: DO NOT delete the chat or block the stalker immediately before backing up the evidence.
Take full-screen screenshots showing user handles, phone numbers, dates, and timestamps.
Lodge an official online complaint at the FIA Cyber Crime Portal (complaint.fia.gov.pk) or call FIA Helpline 1991.
Visit the local FIA Cyber Crime Reporting Center with your CNIC and phone for forensic verification and lodging of FIR.
Seek emergency takedown of content through PTA (Pakistan Telecommunication Authority).

documents.chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
documents.bailable: Non-bailable (Bail is at the discretion of the Court)

documents.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
documents.summary_plain: Applies when someone dishonestly deceives you into giving them money, funds, or property through fraudulent misrepresentations, contractor scams, false promises, or trickery (e.g. taking cash/rupees or advance payment and turning off phone or disappearing).

evidence_required: Bank transfer receipts, deposit slips, or financial transaction logs
Written agreements, MOUs, or receipts showing commitment
Text messages, emails, WhatsApp conversations proving deceitful intent from the inception
Witness testimony of persons present during negotiations or handover of funds/property
practical_steps: Gather all proof of payment (bank statements, cheques, receipts) and written communications.
Send a formal legal notice through an Advocate demanding return of money/property within 14 days.
Lodge a written complaint under Section 154 CrPC at the relevant Police Station for FIR registration.

If the Station House Officer (SHO) refuses to register an FIR, file a petition under Section 22-A / 22-B CrPC before the Ex-Officio Justice of Peace (Sessions Court) seeking a direction for FIR registration.

documents.section_title: Dishonestly issuing a cheque
documents.chapter: Chapter XVIII: Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks
documents.bailable: Bailable (subject to court discretion depending on amount and conduct)
documents.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, unless the drawer can prove that he made arrangements with his bank to ensure the cheque would be honoured and that the bank was at fault.
documents.summary_plain: Applies when someone issues a bank cheque dishonestly towards repayment of a loan or fulfillment of an obligation, and the cheque bounces/dishonours upon presentation due to insufficient funds.
documents.summary_urdu: بدنیتی سے ایسا بینک چیک جاری کرنا جو کھاتے میں ناکافی رقم کی وجہ سے باؤنس (مسترد) ہو جائے۔ یہ قابلِ دست اندازی پولیس جرم ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Whoever dishonestly issues a cheque towards re-payment of a loan or fulfillment of an obligation which is dishonoured on presentation, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, unless he can establish, for which burden of proof shall rest on him, that he had made arrangements with his bank to ensure that the cheque would be honoured and that the bank was at fault in not honouring the cheque.
evidence_required: Original bounced cheque
Bank Return Memo / Dishonour Slip showing reason (e.g., 'Funds Insufficient' or 'Account Closed')
Proof of underlying consideration/obligation (agreement, invoice, ledger, loan receipt)
Copy of written Legal Notice served on the drawer demanding payment, with postal courier receipts/TCS tracking
practical_steps: Obtain the original cheque and bank return memo from your bank immediately.
Engage an Advocate to dispatch a statutory Legal Demand Notice to the issuer within a reasonable period giving 7-14 days to clear the debt.
Submit an application to the local Police Station within whose jurisdiction the bank branch is situated to register an FIR under Section 489-F PPC.
If the police delay or refuse, file an application under Section 22-A / 22-B CrPC before the Sessions Judge / Justice of Peace.

documents.section_title: Criminal breach of trust and punishment
documents.chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
documents.compoundable: Compoundable with permission of the Court
documents.punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both under Section 406 PPC.
documents.summary_plain: Applies when money, property, or company funds are entrusted to someone (such as a business partner, director, employee, agent, trustee, custodian, or borrower), and that person dishonestly misappropriates it, uses company accounts for personal expenses, converts funds to personal use without authorization, or disposes of it in violation of law or agreement.
documents.summary_urdu: امانت میں خیانت (دفعہ 405 و 406 تعزیرات پاکستان)۔ جب کوئی بزنس پارٹنر، ملازم یا ٹرسٹی کمپنی کے فنڈز یا امانت میں رکھی گئی رقم کو اپنے ذاتی خرچ یا ذاتی فائدے کے لیے غیر قانونی طور پر استعمال کرے تو یہ سنگین فوجداری جرم ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 405: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged... commits criminal breach of trust. Section 406: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
evidence_required: Documentary proof of entrustment, partnership deed, business agreement, or employment contract
Company bank account statements showing unauthorized transfers or withdrawals for personal expenses
Financial audit report, transaction receipts, or account ledgers demonstrating misappropriation of funds
Written demand notice requesting accounting and reimbursement of company funds with proof of dispatch
Witness testimony, communication records, or partner resolutions regarding fund usage
practical_steps: Issue a formal written legal notice demanding full financial reconciliation and restitution of misused company funds within 14 days.
Gather certified bank account records, partnership deeds, and audit evidence proving unauthorized diversion of business funds for personal expenses.
Lodge a formal written complaint with the local police station under Section 154 CrPC for registration of an FIR under Section 406 PPC.
If police fail or refuse to register the case, file a private criminal complaint (Istighasa) under Section 200 CrPC before the Judicial Magistrate or petition under Section 22-A CrPC.
Consider initiating civil recovery proceedings or a suit for dissolution of partnership and rendition of accounts in parallel.

documents.summary_plain: Applies when someone enters another person's land, house, or property without permission with intent to commit an offence, or to intimidate, insult, or annoy the lawful possessor, or unlawfully remains there.
documents.summary_urdu: غیر قانونی دخل اندازی اور مکان میں زبردستی گھسنا۔ بغیر اجازت کسی کی اراضی یا رہائش گاہ میں قبضہ کرنے یا دھمکانے کی غرض سے داخل ہونا۔

Section 447 & 448 provide punishments therefor.
evidence_required: Proof of lawful possession (fard malkiat, registered deed, utility bills in possessor's name)
Photographs, CCTV footage, or eyewitness statements of unauthorized entry
Police 15 emergency call record or complaint log
Proof of intimidation or refusal to vacate

File written complaint under Section 154 CrPC for FIR under 448/447 PPC.
If forcibly dispossessed by land grabbers (qabza mafia), file a complaint under Section 3 of the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 before the Court of Sessions.
File an application under Section 145 CrPC before the Magistrate for sealing or restoring possession to prevent breach of peace.

documents.punishment: Part 1: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine or both. Part 2 (threat to cause death or grievous hurt or destruction of property by fire): Imprisonment up to 7 years, or with fine, or with both.
documents.summary_plain: Applies when someone threatens you with injury to your person, reputation, or property (or to a loved one) with intent to cause alarm, or to force you to do something you are not legally bound to do.

Section 506: Punishment for criminal intimidation...

SMS, WhatsApp messages, social media direct messages containing threats
CCTV footage of confrontational encounters
Eyewitness statements of threats uttered in public or in front of third parties

documents.punishment: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine up to five hundred thousand rupees, or with both.
documents.summary_plain: Protects women against public harassment, stalking, indecent gestures, intrusive words, or exhibition of any object intending that such word or gesture shall be heard or seen by a woman to insult her modesty.
documents.summary_urdu: خواتین کو ہراساں کرنا، غیر اخلاقی اشارے یا الفاظ استعمال کرنا۔ عوامی جگہوں، گلیوں، یا کام کی جگہ پر عورت کی عزت و وقار مجروح کرنے کے خلاف قانونی تحفظ۔

evidence_required: CCTV footage or mobile video recordings
Witness testimony of bystanders or colleagues
Digital messages, photos, or stalking logs
Police complaint copy / 15 call detail
practical_steps: Report immediately to Punjab/Sindh/KP Police Women Protection Helpline (e.g. 1043 in Punjab or 15).
Lodge written complaint at the local Police Station for FIR under Section 509 PPC.

Section: 509 - Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman or harassment
Chapter: Chapter XXII: Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
Category: Criminal Law / Women Protection
Jurisdiction: Federal (Applicable across all Pakistan)
Plain Summary: Protects women against public harassment, stalking, indecent gestures, intrusive words, or exhibition of any object intending that such word or gesture shall be heard or seen by a woman to insult her modesty.
Urdu Summary: خواتین کو ہراساں کرنا، غیر اخلاقی اشارے یا الفاظ استعمال کرنا۔ عوامی جگہوں، گلیوں، یا کام کی جگہ پر عورت کی عزت و وقار مجروح کرنے کے خلاف قانونی تحفظ۔
Court / Forum: Court of Judicial Magistrate / Federal/Provincial Ombudsperson for Protection Against Harassment at the Workplace
Statutory Text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine up to five hundred thousand rupees, or with both.
Evidence Required: CCTV footage or mobile video recordings Witness testimony of bystanders or colleagues Digital messages, photos, or stalking logs Police complaint copy / 15 call detail

documents.section_title: Prohibition of depriving woman from inheriting property and forced marriage
documents.chapter: Chapter XX-A: Of Offences Against Women
documents.punishment: Section 498-A (Depriving of inheritance): Imprisonment up to 10 years and not less than 5 years, or fine of one million rupees, or both. Section 498-B (Forced marriage): Imprisonment up to 7 years and not less than 3 years, and fine of five hundred thousand rupees.
documents.summary_plain: Prohibits depriving any woman of her lawful inheritance through deceit, coercion, or fraud. Also strictly criminalizes forcing a woman into marriage without her free and valid consent.
documents.summary_urdu: عورت کو جائیداد کے وراثتی حق سے محروم کرنے اور زبردستی شادی کروانے کے خلاف سخت قانونی سزا (پانچ سے دس سال قید)۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 498-A: Whoever by deceitful or illegal means deprives any woman from acquiring any property at the time of opening of succession shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to ten years but not less than five years or with fine of one million rupees or both. Section 498-B: Whoever coerces or compels a woman to enter into marriage shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years.

Revenue records (fard, mutation/intiqal) showing alienation of inherited land
Proof of deceit, forged relinquish deeds (Tamleek / Dastbardari nama)
Affidavit of the victim confirming lack of consent
practical_steps: Obtain NADRA FRC and revenue mutation documents showing how the deceased's inheritance was distributed.
File complaint before Sessions Court or Police for registration of FIR under Section 498-A/498-B PPC.
Apply to the Revenue Officer/Assistant Commissioner to challenge and cancel the fraudulent inheritance mutation.
File a declaratory suit in Civil Court under Section 42 Specific Relief Act challenging any forged relinquishment deed.

documents.chapter: Chapter XVI: Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
documents.compoundable: Compoundable with permission of the Court

Engage an Advocate to monitor police investigation and ensure recovery of crime weapon.

documents.section_title: Robbery, attempted robbery, and armed robbery with deadly weapons
documents.chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
documents.punishment: Section 392: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years (14 years if on highway between sunset and sunrise) and fine. Section 393: Attempted robbery is punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years and fine. Section 397: Armed robbery/attempt with deadly weapon carries mandatory minimum 7 years imprisonment.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 392 PPC, robbery is committed when theft or extortion is accompanied by causing or attempting to cause death, hurt, or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant hurt. Under Section 393 PPC, even if no money, cash, medicine, or goods were successfully stolen (such as an attempted armed robbery at a pharmacy, shop, or home where the culprits were scared off, resisted, or fled), the mere attempt to commit robbery is a severe non-bailable cognizable crime punishable by up to 7 years rigorous imprisonment. Section 397 mandates minimum 7-year imprisonment if a deadly weapon (gun, pistol) is used.
documents.summary_urdu: ڈکیتی، رہزنی اور اقدامِ ڈکیتی (دفعات 392، 393 و 397)۔ اگر مسلح افراد دکان، میڈیکل اسٹور یا گھر میں گن پوائنٹ پر لوٹ مار کی کوشش کریں لیکن کچھ لوٹ نہ سکیں، تب بھی اقدامِ ڈکیتی (دفعہ 393) کے تحت 7 سال تک قیدِ بامشقت کی سزا ہوتی ہے اور اسلحہ لہرانے پر دفعہ 397 کے تحت کم از کم 7 سال قید لازمی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 392: Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the robbery be committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years. Section 393: Whoever attempts to commit robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Section 397: If, at the time of committing robbery or dacoity, the offender uses any deadly weapon, or causes grievous hurt to any person, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years.
evidence_required: CCTV footage from inside and outside the premises showing armed culprits
Immediate 15 police emergency call record and dispatch log
Eyewitness statements of shopkeeper, staff, or bystanders
Empty bullet casings, discarded weapons, or vehicle license plates noted
Medico-Legal Certificate (MLC) if any physical scuffle or injury occurred
practical_steps: Immediately dial Police Emergency 15 to log the incident and ensure police visit the crime scene.
Preserve and download CCTV camera footage showing armed perpetrators and weapons.
Visit the local police station and submit a written application for immediate registration of FIR under Sections 393/397/34 PPC.
If the SHO refuses to lodge an FIR, file a petition under Section 22-A & 22-B CrPC before the Sessions Judge / Ex-Officio Justice of Peace.
Attend the identification parade before a Judicial Magistrate if police arrest suspects.

documents.act_title: Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860)
documents.section_title: Rash driving on public way and hurt caused by rash or negligent driving (Road Accidents)
documents.chapter: Chapter XIV & XVI: Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety & Human Body
documents.compoundable: Compoundable with permission of the Court
documents.punishment: Section 279: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to 3,000 rupees, or both. Section 337-G: Arsh or Daman (monetary compensation) specified for the injury, and imprisonment up to 5 years as Ta'zir.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 279 PPC, driving any vehicle on a public way so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or safety is a criminal offence. If physical hurt or injury is caused to any person by such rash or negligent driving, Section 337-G PPC applies, holding the driver criminally liable to pay Daman/Arsh (compensation) and undergo imprisonment up to 5 years. In addition, claims for vehicular damage and third-party insurance compensation can be brought before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) or civil courts.
documents.summary_urdu: تیز رفتاری اور غفلت سے گاڑی چلانے پر حادثہ اور چوٹ (دفعات 279 اور 337-جی)۔ سڑک پر تیز رفتاری یا لاپرواہی سے گاڑی چلا کر حادثہ کرنے پر 2 سال تک قید اور چوٹ پہنچنے پر دیت/ارش/ضمان اور 5 سال تک قید کی سزا ہو سکتی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ موٹر ایکسیڈنٹ ٹربیونل سے مالی معاوضہ طلب کیا جا سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 279: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to three thousand rupees, or with both. Section 337-G: Whoever causes hurt by rash or negligent driving shall be liable to the arsh or daman specified for the kind of hurt caused and may also be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years as ta'zir.
evidence_required: Police 15 emergency call and First Information Report (FIR) under 279/337-G
Medico-Legal Certificate (MLC) from Government Hospital detailing injuries
Motor Vehicle Examiner (MVE) inspection report of both vehicles
Photographs and video of accident spot, skid marks, and vehicular damage
practical_steps: Ensure immediate medical assistance and obtain a Medico-Legal Certificate (MLC) from a government hospital.
Call Police 15 and register an FIR under Section 279 and 337-G PPC at the local police station.
Obtain an official mechanical inspection report from the Motor Vehicle Examiner (MVE).
File a claim for vehicular damage and injury compensation before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) or Insurance Tribunal.

documents.section_title: Theft and Theft in Dwelling House or Building
documents.chapter: Chapter XVII: Of Offences Against Property
documents.compoundable: Compoundable with permission of the Court and consent of owner
documents.punishment: Section 379: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Section 380: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 378 and 379 PPC, whoever intends to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent commits theft, punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment. If the theft is committed in any building, tent, or vessel used as a human dwelling or for custody of property (such as stealing cash, jewelry, or valuables from a home or bedroom drawer), Section 380 PPC applies, carrying an enhanced punishment of up to 7 years imprisonment and fine. The offense is cognizable, requiring the local police to register an FIR upon complaint.
documents.summary_urdu: چوری اور گھر یا عمارت سے چوری (دفعات 378، 379 اور 380)۔ کسی کی اجازت کے بغیر اس کی رقم، نقدی، زیورات یا سامان چرانا جرم ہے۔ عام چوری پر 3 سال قید اور گھر یا کمرے سے چوری (دفعہ 380) پر 7 سال تک قید اور جرمانہ ہے۔ یہ ایک قابلِ دست اندازی پولیس جرم ہے جس پر فوری ایف آئی آر درج کی جاتی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 378: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft. Section 379: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Section 380: Whoever commits theft in any building, tent or vessel, which building, tent or vessel is used as a human dwelling, or used for the custody of property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
evidence_required: Prompt emergency call to Police 15 and First Information Report (FIR) under Section 380 PPC
List, inventory, and purchase receipts or proofs of stolen cash, jewelry, or electronics
CCTV footage, mobile phone records, or eyewitness testimony showing unauthorized entry or departure
Crime scene inspection memo and forensic fingerprint lifting by police investigation team
practical_steps: Immediately dial Police 15 to report the theft and secure the crime scene.
Visit the local police station with a written application detailing the stolen items and suspects to register an FIR under Section 380 PPC.
Provide police with an inventory memo of stolen items, serial numbers, CCTV footage, or eyewitness details.
If the SHO refuses to lodge the FIR, file an application before the Ex-Officio Justice of the Peace / Sessions Court under Section 22-A CrPC.
Upon arrest and recovery of stolen property, file a superdari application under Section 516-A CrPC to obtain temporary custody of recovered cash or items.

documents.section_title: Burden of proof
documents.chapter: Part III, Chapter VII: Of the Burden of Proof
documents.punishment: A party that fails to discharge its burden of proof loses the lawsuit or criminal charge.
documents.summary_plain: The foundational rule of evidence: 'He who asserts must prove.' In criminal cases, the prosecution bears the heavy burden of proving guilt beyond reasonable doubt. In civil cases, the plaintiff must prove their case on a preponderance of probabilities.
