documents.statutory_text: Article 117: Whoever desires any Court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts which he asserts, must prove that those facts exist. When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person. Article 118: The burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lies on that person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side.
evidence_required: Primary original documents whenever available
Reliable witness testimony corroborating material assertions
Public documents, certified official copies, and revenue extracts
practical_steps: Identify exactly which party holds the legal burden for each specific issue framed by the court.
Ensure all essential facts are supported by admissible oral and documentary proof.
Capitalize on contradictions in the opponent's case to demonstrate failure of proof.

documents.section_title: Confession to police officer not to be proved
documents.chapter: Part II, Chapter III: Admissions and Confessions
documents.category: Law of Evidence / Protection Against Police Torture
documents.punishment: Any statement or confession extracted while in police custody is completely inadmissible in evidence against the accused.
documents.summary_plain: Under Pakistani law, any confession made to a police officer, or made while in police custody (unless made in the immediate presence of a Judicial Magistrate under Section 164 CrPC), is strictly inadmissible in court. This protects citizens against coerced confessions obtained through police torture or custodial pressure.
documents.summary_urdu: پولیس کے سامنے اعترافِ جرم کی عدم قبولیت۔ پولیس کے سامنے یا پولیس حراست میں دیا گیا کوئی بھی بیان یا اقبالِ جرم عدالت میں قابلِ قبول ثبوت نہیں ہے، تاوقتیکہ وہ مجسٹریٹ کے روبرو دفعہ 164 کے تحت نہ ہو۔
documents.statutory_text: Article 38: No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence. Article 39: Subject to Article 40, no confession made by any person whilst he is in the custody of a police officer, unless it be made in the immediate presence of a Magistrate, shall be proved as against such person.
evidence_required: Proof that the statement was made to or recorded by a police officer or while in custody
Absence of voluntary judicial certificate by Magistrate under Section 164 CrPC
Medical evidence of custodial torture / bruising if applicable
practical_steps: Advocate must object to any attempt by prosecution to introduce alleged police station admissions.
If forced to sign blank papers in police lockup, immediately inform the Magistrate when produced for physical remand.
Demand immediate Medico-Legal examination if subjected to custodial abuse.

documents.act_title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
documents.section_title: Competence and number of witnesses
documents.chapter: Part I, Chapter II: Of Witnesses
documents.category: Law of Evidence / Witness Testimony & Proof
documents.punishment: A criminal conviction cannot stand if the sole witness is uncorroborated, interested, or fails the test of credibility.
documents.summary_plain: Under Article 17 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, while the law generally states that no particular number of witnesses is required for the proof of any fact, in serious criminal allegations the courts mandate extraordinary caution when evaluating a solitary witness. A single uncorroborated oral witness, especially in charges involving verbal remarks overheard by a single person, is subject to strict judicial scrutiny and must be corroborated by independent evidence to establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
documents.summary_urdu: گواہوں کی اہلیت اور تعداد (آرٹیکل 17)۔ قانون شہادت کے تحت کسی بھی معاملے میں گواہوں کی کوئی خاص تعداد لازمی نہیں ہے، لیکن سنگین فوجداری الزامات میں محض ایک ہی گواہ کی سنی سنائی بات پر سزا نہیں دی جا سکتی۔ عدالت ایسے واحد گواہ کے بیان کی سخت چھان بین اور آزادانہ تائیدی ثبوت کا مطالبہ کرتی ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Article 17: (1) The competence of a person to testify, and the number of witnesses required in any case, shall be determined in accordance with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran and Sunnah: (2) Unless otherwise provided in any law relating to the enforcement of Hudood or any other special law: (a) In matters pertaining to financial or future obligations, if reduced to writing, the instrument shall be attested by two men, or one man and two women, so that one may remind the other; and (b) in all other matters, the Court may accept, or act on, the testimony of one man or one woman or such other evidence as the circumstances of the case may warrant.
evidence_required: Proof of motive, background enmity, or grudge of the solitary witness
Material contradictions between initial complaint and court statement
Absence of independent corroborative evidence or audio/recording
Proof of location and physical impossibility of overhearing
practical_steps: Cross-examine the sole prosecution witness extensively on their exact position, distance, background noise, and prior relationship with the parties.
Demonstrate any prior hostility, disputes, or affiliations between the witness and the complainant.
Highlight the complete lack of independent corroboration by neutral neighbors or bystanders.
Rely on established Superior Court precedents holding that solitary overheard evidence without corroboration cannot justify criminal conviction.

documents.act_title: Punjab Rented Premises Act (Act VII of 2009)
documents.section_title: Application for eviction / ejectment of tenant
documents.chapter: Eviction Proceedings
documents.punishment: Warrant of eviction executed through police force if tenant does not vacate within 30 days of final order.
documents.summary_plain: In Punjab, a landlord can file an eviction application before the Special Rent Tribunal on statutory grounds: (a) expiry of tenancy period; (b) tenant's failure to pay rent within the agreed date or within 30 days after due date; (c) breach of tenancy agreement terms; (d) tenant subletting without written consent; (e) tenant causing damage to premises; or (f) landlord's bona fide personal need.
documents.summary_urdu: پنجاب میں کرایہ دار کی بے دخلی کا طریقہ کار (دفعہ 15)۔ کرایہ ادا نہ کرنے، کرایہ داری کی مدت ختم ہونے، یا مالک مکان کی ذاتی ضرورت کی بنیاد پر رینٹ ٹربیونل سے فوری بے دخلی کا حکم حاصل کیا جا سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 15: A landlord may apply for the eviction of a tenant if: (a) the period of tenancy has expired; (b) the tenant has failed to pay or tender rent within the agreed period, or in the absence of an agreement, within thirty days from the due date; (c) the tenant has committed breach of a term or condition of the tenancy agreement; (d) the tenant has committed an act likely to impair the material value or utility of the premises; (e) the tenant has used the premises for a purpose other than that for which it was let out; (f) the tenant has sub-let the premises without written consent; or (g) the landlord requires the premises in good faith for his own use or for the use of any of his children.
evidence_required: Registered Tenancy Agreement or tenancy recorded with Rent Registrar
Notice of eviction or default served on tenant with proof of dispatch
Bank statements or rent receipt book showing non-payment or default
Proof of personal bona fide need (if claimed on ground of personal use)
practical_steps: Ensure tenancy agreement is registered with the local Rent Registrar (otherwise pay 5-10% fine under Section 5).
Serve formal notice to tenant demanding arrears of rent or surrender of vacant possession.
File Eviction Application under Section 15 PRPA before the Special Rent Tribunal.
Under Section 19 PRPA, tenant must obtain 'Leave to Contest' within 10 days of service, failing which eviction order is passed automatically.
Execute eviction through Rent Tribunal's bailiff with police assistance.

documents.act_title: Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance (Ordinance XVII of 1979)
documents.section_title: Application to Controller for eviction of tenant
documents.chapter: Eviction Proceedings
documents.jurisdiction: Provincial (Sindh Province - Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur, etc.)
documents.punishment: Eviction order executable as civil decree by Rent Controller.
documents.summary_plain: In Sindh, a landlord cannot evict a tenant except by applying to the Rent Controller on grounds such as: (a) default in rent payment exceeding 60 days from the due date; (b) subletting premises without landlord's written consent; (c) acts causing nuisance or impairing building value; (d) bona fide personal requirement of landlord or spouse/children.
documents.summary_urdu: سندھ میں کرایہ دار کے خلاف بے دخلی کی کارروائی (دفعہ 15)۔ 60 دن سے زائد کرایہ ادا نہ کرنے، بلا اجازت ذیلی کرایہ دار رکھنے، یا مالک کی ذاتی ضرورت پر رینٹ کنٹرولر سے رجوع کیا جاتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 15(2): The Controller may, on an application by the landlord, make an order directing the tenant to put the landlord in possession of the premises if he is satisfied that: (i) the tenant has failed to pay or tender the rent within sixty days; (ii) the tenant has handed over possession to another person without consent; (iii) the tenant has committed acts likely to impair the utility of the premises; (vii) the landlord requires the premises in good faith for his own occupation or use of spouse or children.
evidence_required: Tenancy agreement signed by both parties
Bank deposit slips / money order receipts showing default
Notice of demand and postal courier slips
Proof of bona fide personal need
practical_steps: Send a legal notice via registered mail specifying default of over 60 days.
File Eviction Case under Section 15 SRPO before the Rent Controller having territorial jurisdiction.
Rent Controller directs tenant to deposit tentative rent arrears under Section 16 SRPO.
If tenant fails to deposit rent on the court's date, tenant's defense is struck off and immediate eviction is ordered.

documents.punishment: Eviction order executable as a decree of the civil court through the Bailiff of Islamabad Civil Courts.

Act: Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance (Ordinance IV of 2001) (IRRO)
Section: Section 17 - Eviction of tenant in Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT)
Chapter: Eviction Proceedings
Category: Property Law / Tenancy
Jurisdiction: Federal (Islamabad Capital Territory - ICT)
Plain Summary: In Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT), eviction of a tenant is governed exclusively by the Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance 2001, NOT Punjab or Sindh rent laws. A landlord must apply to the Rent Controller, Islamabad, on statutory grounds: (a) default in rent payment for more than 15 days after due date; (b) expiry of agreed lease period; (c) subletting without landlord's written consent; (d) damage to premises or nuisance; or (e) personal bona fide need of landlord or family. Landlords in Islamabad cannot forcefully evict or change locks without an order from the Rent Controller.
Urdu Summary: اسلام آباد میں کرایہ دار کی بے دخلی کا قانون (اسلام آباد رینٹ ریسٹرکشن آرڈیننس 2001 دفعہ 17)۔ وفاقی دارالحکومت اسلام آباد میں پنجاب یا سندھ کا قانون لاگو نہیں ہوتا۔ رینٹ کنٹرولر اسلام آباد کی عدالت سے 15 دن سے زائد کرایہ ادا نہ کرنے یا مدت ختم ہونے پر بے دخلی کا حکم لیا جاتا ہے۔
Court / Forum: Court of Rent Controller, Islamabad (Civil Courts, Islamabad Capital Territory)
Statutory Text: Section 17: A landlord who seeks to evict his tenant shall apply to the Controller for a direction in that behalf. The Controller may make an order directing the tenant to put the landlord in possession if satisfied that: (i) the tenant has not paid or tendered rent within fifteen days after due date; (ii) the tenant has transferred his right under the lease or sub-let the building without written permission; (iii) the tenant has committed acts likely to impair the utility of the building; (iv) the landlord requires it in good faith for his own occupation or that of his children.
Evidence Required: Tenancy agreement registered or executed in Islamabad Rent payment bank receipts or cash vouchers Notice of demand or default served in Islamabad Allotment letter or CDA ownership record in Islamabad sectors
Practical Steps: Confirm jurisdiction lies before the Rent Controller Islamabad (Civil Courts ICT, G-10 or F-8). Serve formal notice to tenant under Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance 2001. File Eviction Petition under Section 17 IRRO 2001 before the Rent Controller Islamabad. Rent Controller determines tentative rent under Section 18 IRRO 2001. Execute final eviction order through Court Bailiff of Islamabad Civil Courts.

documents.act_title: Punjab Rented Premises Act (Act VII of 2009)
documents.section_title: Refund of advance rent and security deposit upon vacation of premises
documents.chapter: Obligations of Landlord and Rights of Tenant
documents.punishment: Order directing landlord to refund the security deposit with costs; executable as a civil decree by the Rent Tribunal.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 13 of the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009, a landlord is legally required to refund the tenant the security deposit or advance rent within thirty days of the date on which the tenant vacates the premises, after deducting any proven arrears of rent or utility bills. If the landlord fails or refuses to return the security deposit, the tenant has the statutory right to file an application before the Rent Tribunal for the recovery of the deposit amount.
documents.summary_urdu: سیکیورٹی ڈپازٹ اور ایڈوانس کرایہ کی واپسی (پنجاب رینٹڈ پریمسز ایکٹ 2009 دفعہ 13)۔ مکان یا دکان خالی کرنے کے 30 دن کے اندر مالک مکان پر سیکیورٹی ڈپازٹ واپس کرنا قانونی طور پر لازم ہے۔ انکار کی صورت میں کرایہ دار رینٹ ٹربیونل میں وصولی کی درخواست دائر کر سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 13: (1) A landlord shall refund to the tenant the advance rent or the security deposit within thirty days of the date on which the tenant vacates the premises after deducting any arrears of rent or utility bills or cost of damage caused to the premises. (2) If the landlord fails to refund the advance rent or security deposit, the tenant may file an application before the Rent Tribunal for the recovery of the amount.
evidence_required: Tenancy agreement showing amount of security deposit paid
Bank deposit slip, cheque, or receipt acknowledging receipt of security deposit by landlord
Proof of handing over vacant possession (keys handover memo, written notice, or witness statements)
Clearance certificates / receipts showing all utility bills and rent up to vacation date are cleared
practical_steps: Serve a written notice on the landlord demanding refund of the security deposit within 30 days of vacating.
Gather receipts showing all rent arrears and utility bills have been fully paid.
If the landlord refuses or delays beyond 30 days, file an application under Section 13 PRPA before the Special Rent Tribunal.
Execute the refund order through the Rent Tribunal under Section 22 PRPA.

documents.act_title: Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance (Ordinance XVII of 1979)
documents.section_title: Prohibition of fine, premium, or unlawful retention of security deposit
documents.chapter: Rents and Security Deposits
documents.punishment: Order of Rent Controller directing refund of security deposit; civil suit for recovery and damages under Contract Act.
documents.summary_plain: Under Sindh rent laws and the law of contract, a landlord cannot unlawfully withhold or forfeit a tenant's security deposit after the tenant has vacated the premises and cleared all dues. The tenant can file an application before the Rent Controller or a civil suit for recovery of money and unjust enrichment under Section 70 and 73 of the Contract Act 1872.

documents.statutory_text: Section 7: No landlord shall claim or receive any premium or other like sum in addition to fair rent or unlawfully retain any security deposit beyond adjustment of lawful dues upon surrender of possession.
evidence_required: Tenancy contract mentioning security deposit
Proof of vacation and utility clearance
Bank statements or payment receipts
practical_steps: Send formal demand notice to landlord requesting return of security deposit.
File claim before Rent Controller or Civil Suit for Recovery of Money under Contract Act 1872.
Attach proof of possession handover and bill clearances.

documents.act_title: Specific Relief Act (Act I of 1877)
documents.section_title: Recovery of possession of specific immovable property
documents.chapter: Part II, Chapter I: Of Recovering Possession of Property
documents.punishment: Decree restoring actual physical possession of land, house, or commercial shop to dispossessed lawful occupant.
documents.summary_plain: Under Section 9, if anyone is dispossessed of immovable property without their consent otherwise than in due course of law, they can file a suit to recover possession within 6 months, even without proving their title or ownership. Section 8 provides recovery based on title/ownership.
documents.summary_urdu: غیر قانونی بے دخلی پر جائیداد کا قبضہ واپس حاصل کرنا (دفعات 8 اور 9)۔ اگر کسی کو زبردستی بغیر قانونی کارروائی بے دخل کیا جائے تو وہ 6 ماہ کے اندر اندر بغیر ملکیت ثابت کیے صرف سابقہ قبضے کی بنیاد پر قبضہ بحال کروا سکتا ہے۔
documents.statutory_text: Section 9: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit. Nothing in this section shall bar any person from suing to establish his title to such property and to recover possession thereof. Suit must be filed within 6 months from date of dispossession.
evidence_required: Proof of prior peaceful physical possession (utility bills, receipts, tenancy deed, tax chalan)
Proof of forcible dispossession without court decree
Police report or 15 emergency call log recorded at the time of illegal dispossession
practical_steps: Calculate 6-month limitation strictly from the exact date of dispossession.
Engage an Advocate to file a Suit for Possession under Section 9 Specific Relief Act.
Obtain ad-interim restraining order preventing the illegal possessor from creating third-party interest or altering the structure.
Upon decree, execute possession through Court Bailiff under Order XXI Rule 35 CPC.

documents.act_title: Specific Relief Act (Act I of 1877)
documents.section_title: Discretion of Court as to declaration of status or right (Suit for Declaration)
documents.chapter: Part II, Chapter VI: Of Declaratory Decrees
documents.punishment: Binding judicial declaration settling disputed ownership, legal character, or inheritance rights.
documents.summary_plain: Used when someone denies or is interested in denying your legal character or right to any property (e.g. disputing your ownership, claiming forged inheritance, or asserting a fraudulent sale deed). The plaintiff asks the civil court to formally declare their rightful title.
documents.summary_urdu: استقرارِ حق کا دعویٰ (ڈیکلریشن آف ٹائٹل - دفعہ 42)۔ جب کوئی مخالف فریق آپ کی جائیداد کی ملکیت سے انکار کرے یا جعلی دستاویزات بنا لے، تو سول کورٹ سے اصل مالکانہ حقوق کا حتمی عدالتی اعلان حاصل کرنا۔
documents.statutory_text: Any person entitled to any legal character, or to any right as to any property, may institute a suit against any person denying, or interested to deny, his title to such character or right, and the Court may in its discretion make therein a declaration that he is so entitled, and the plaintiff need not in such suit ask for any further relief: Provided that no Court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of title, omits to do so.
evidence_required: Registered Sale Deed, Gift Deed (Hiba-nama), or Revenue Mutation (Intiqal)
NADRA Family Registration Certificate (FRC) for inheritance disputes
Revenue Fard Malkiat (Record of Rights) from Land Revenue Authority
Proof of defendant's denial or competing bogus claim
practical_steps: Draft Plaint for Declaration with Consequential Relief (Injunction under Sec 54 and/or Possession).
Attach attested copies of title deeds and revenue record.
Obtain temporary injunction under Order 39 Rules 1 & 2 CPC restraining alienation during suit.
Produce revenue patwari and sub-registrar as official witnesses during evidence stage.
